name: Nintendo Wii U
summary: Explore Wii U hardware and the routes into Aroma custom firmware, from the browser exploit to the optional ISFShax coldboot install, on Basic and Deluxe consoles.

specs.cpu: IBM Espresso, 3 PowerPC 750-based cores at 1.243 GHz
specs.gpu: AMD Latte (Radeon-based) at 550 MHz, HDMI output up to 1080p
specs.memory: 2 GB DDR3 for games and system, plus 32 MB MEM1
specs.storage: 8 GB (Basic) or 32 GB (Deluxe/Premium) internal flash; external USB storage supported
specs.display: TV output up to 1080p; GamePad with a 6.2 in 854×480 resistive touchscreen
specs.media: Wii U 25 GB optical discs; Wii discs in the same drive

variants.notes: WUP-001. White console with one GamePad; the basic set omits the stands and charging cradle. Same hardware generation as the Deluxe, so the homebrew routes are identical.

specs.storage: 8 GB eMMC NAND; external USB storage supported

variants.notes: WUP-101. Black console; the original set adds stands, a charging cradle and a pack-in game, and later bundles change the contents but not the hardware. The extra storage matters because Wii U games and updates are large.

specs.storage: 32 GB eMMC NAND; external USB storage supported

homebrew.name: Wii U browser exploit
homebrew.firmware: The region's latest version or below: 5.5.6 U, 5.5.5 E, 5.5.5 J
homebrew.summary: Runs a payload from the console's Internet Browser, which is how the current guide starts a stock console. It needs internet access and a console at or below its region's latest system version.

compatibility.note: The guide states it works on all Wii U consoles in all regions on the latest firmware for the region or below. That number is 5.5.6 U in North America, 5.5.5 E in Europe and 5.5.5 J in Japan, so no single version list is claimed here: check the exact number in the console's System Settings. Both models are the same hardware generation, so the route does not split by model.

requirements: A Wii U with internet access and its Internet Browser.
An SD card prepared with the Aroma payload files.
The console at its region's latest system version or below.
warnings: Hold B while the exploit page loads to reach the EnvironmentLoader menu, as the guide instructs; releasing early lands in the wrong menu.
If the console freezes on a white screen, reboot it, reset the browser's save data and retry.
Do not follow this route on a console that already has CBHC, Haxchi or Indexiine; the guide requires uninstalling those first.

homebrew.name: PayloadLoader (Health and Safety autoboot)
homebrew.firmware: Any version; installed from a browser-exploit session and not tied to one firmware
homebrew.summary: Installs the payload loader onto the Health and Safety Information app, so the SD-card environment can start without the browser. The guide installs it after taking a NAND backup.

compatibility.note: Installed through the browser exploit and then started by launching the Health and Safety Information app. Upstream publishes an installer rather than a firmware matrix.

requirements: A NAND backup already taken with the guide's dumper.
A browser-exploit session on the same console to run the installer.
warnings: A factory reset does not remove the injected PayloadLoader; use the guide's uninstall page instead.
Uninstalling it is the documented way back to a stock boot.

homebrew.name: Aroma
homebrew.firmware: The region's latest version: 5.5.6 U, 5.5.5 E, 5.5.5 J (Aroma's README names 5.5.5/5.5.6 without splitting it by region)
homebrew.summary: The current homebrew environment: modules, plugins, WUHB homebrew and region-free patches, started by EnvironmentLoader. It replaces Tiramisu, and old .elf homebrew plus the old Homebrew Launcher do not work under it.

compatibility.note: Aroma's README names the latest firmware (5.5.5/5.5.6) without splitting it by region: the current number is 5.5.6 U in North America, 5.5.5 E in Europe and 5.5.5 J in Japan, and the guide describes homebrew and CFW working on the latest version or below. No exact universal version list is claimed; older versions are untested for Aroma itself. It also states a persistent entrypoint with installer and coldboot option, and support for existing entrypoints such as the browser exploit.

requirements: EnvironmentLoader and the Aroma files on the SD card, as the guide's SD preparation step lays out.
PayloadLoader or the browser exploit to start the environment.
warnings: The guide calls Aroma a beta release; not every upstream feature has been tested.
Old .elf homebrew and the Homebrew Launcher no longer work under Aroma; Tiramisu remains for those.
Aroma and Tiramisu are alternatives, not layers; follow one guide end to end.
Boot behaviour depends on the SD card being FAT32; the guide warns not to label the card "wiiu".

homebrew.name: EnvironmentLoader
homebrew.firmware: Any version; runs after an entry exploit
homebrew.summary: The menu that lists the environments on the SD card under sd:/wiiu/environments/ and starts the selected one. Holding X on the GamePad while it loads forces the menu open.

compatibility.note: Upstream documents the SD layout and the X-for-menu behaviour rather than a firmware matrix; it is a payload started by another exploit.

requirements: An entry exploit to run the payload.
At least one environment directory on the SD card.
warnings: Setup payloads must not call exit, and they run in filename order; a bad module can stop the boot chain.

homebrew.name: ISFShax (coldboot boot1)
homebrew.firmware: Any version; installed from an existing homebrew entry and runs before IOSU
homebrew.summary: A coldboot boot1 exploit that installs into the SLC and loads a stage-2 payload (minute_minute) before IOSU. It allows early patches, brick repair and coldbooting other environments, at the cost of a permanent, risky NAND write.

compatibility.note: Upstream publishes no firmware matrix; ISFShax is installed from an existing entry and loads before IOSU. The setup guide treats it as a permanent change to the SLC.

requirements: A full SLC backup and a tested way to restore it (de_Fuse or an SLC hardmod) before installing.
An existing way to run the installer; the setup guide uses Haxchi as entry or Aroma with wafel_installer.
warnings: A broken ISFS superblock write can brick the console; only use a superblock that has been tested and confirmed working.
The stage-2 payload tries the SD card, then the SLC, then an IOSU fallback; a missing SD payload is recoverable, a bad SLC write is not.
Restoring an SLC backup taken before the install removes ISFShax.
A boot1 update from Nintendo would brick a console with ISFShax, so boot1 updates are blocked by a plugin while it is installed.

homebrew.name: Tiramisu
homebrew.summary: The previous environment: Mocha plus the Homebrew Launcher and an autoboot menu. Upstream calls it a legacy environment, and the current guide moves users to Aroma instead.

compatibility.note: Upstream describes Tiramisu as a modular legacy environment loaded by EnvironmentLoader; it does not publish a firmware matrix.

requirements: EnvironmentLoader on the SD card.
The Tiramisu setup modules and Homebrew Launcher files placed as upstream describes.
warnings: Some homebrew still needs Tiramisu, but upstream labels it legacy and the guide recommends Aroma.
Do not run Tiramisu and Aroma as layers; pick one environment per setup.

homebrew.name: Haxchi, CBHC and Indexiine (legacy launchers)
homebrew.firmware: Any version; legacy launchers the current guide removes
homebrew.summary: Older userland CFW launchers that the current guide uninstalls before an Aroma setup. CBHC in particular writes to a system title, so its removal is a documented procedure rather than deleting files.

compatibility.note: The guide documents removal, not installation: CBHC, Haxchi and Indexiine users are told to uninstall before following the Aroma guide.

requirements: Read the guide's uninstall page for the launcher already installed.
warnings: Do not install Aroma over CBHC, Haxchi or Indexiine; uninstall the old launcher first.
Deleting CBHC files instead of following the uninstall page can leave the console unable to boot.

homebrew.name: NAND backup (nanddumper)
homebrew.firmware: Any version; run from the browser-exploit session
homebrew.summary: Dumps the console's NAND to the SD card before PayloadLoader or any deeper change. The guide has the backup taken before the installer writes to the system.

compatibility.note: The guide runs the dumper from the browser exploit and treats the resulting backup as the recovery baseline; it does not publish a firmware matrix.

requirements: An SD card large enough to hold the console's NAND dump.
The browser-exploit session that starts the dumper.
warnings: The backup is only useful together with a way to restore it; keep a copy off the console.
A backup belongs to the console it came from and does not transfer to another Wii U.

homebrew.name: Nintendo Wii U system update
homebrew.summary: Nintendo's own system update, which installs the current release and can repair system software on a console that still boots. It removes homebrew and cannot repair a bad boot1 write.

compatibility.note: Nintendo's US update history lists 5.5.6 U above 5.5.5 U, and Nintendo Japan lists 5.5.5 J as the current version; Europe's latest is 5.5.5 E. The official path installs the current release for the console's region only, so the version depends on the region rather than on one universal number.

requirements: A console that still boots far enough to reach System Settings or the update prompt.
Internet access, or Nintendo's documented update method.
warnings: There is no vendor downgrade; the update path installs the current release.
An update or system repair removes homebrew and does not repair a bad boot1 write.

homebrew.name: Wii U firmware rollback status — no verified general method
homebrew.firmware: No general rollback method documented; Nintendo ships updates forward-only (final: 5.5.6 U, 5.5.5 E, 5.5.5 J)
homebrew.summary: Records the Wii U limit: Nintendo publishes no downgrade and delivers updates forward-only, so an older system version is not an official option. Community NAND tools are repair paths for one console.

compatibility.note: No model-specific rollback method was verified; the guide and Nintendo's update history describe updates only.

warnings: NAND tools such as minute, de_Fuse and ISFShax are recovery tools, not a version selector.
A restored NAND backup belongs to the console it came from.

homebrew.name: Homebrew App Store
homebrew.firmware: Runs from the Homebrew Launcher under Aroma or Tiramisu; no firmware matrix is published.
homebrew.summary: A GUI store for open-source Wii U homebrew, with browsing, downloads and updates from the console.

compatibility.note: README: place it in sd:/wiiu/apps/appstore and run it from the Homebrew Launcher; the console needs a working homebrew environment.

requirements: A Wii U with homebrew access and the Homebrew Launcher (Aroma or Tiramisu).
An SD card for the app and its downloads.
warnings: Only lists open-source homebrew; review each app before installing it.
homebrew.availability: Open source (GPL-3.0); releases published by the project.

homebrew.name: linux-wiiu
homebrew.firmware: Install guide assumes Cafe OS homebrew (Aroma) and states no model or firmware limit.
homebrew.summary: A Linux port for the Wii U that exposes the console hardware from a normal Linux environment. Distributions include Adélie, ArchPOWER, Debian and Gentoo, booted through petitboot.

compatibility.note: Install guide targets the Wii U with Aroma homebrew and gives no model or firmware restriction.

requirements: A Wii U with Aroma homebrew working.
An SD card for the bootloader plus a USB drive, SD partition or SATA device for the distribution.
warnings: Flashable disk images erase the target device; the guide warns before each destructive step.
Performance depends on the storage medium; USB 2.0 is slow, SD or SATA is recommended.
homebrew.availability: Open source; distribution images published by the project.
